approach: Root cause: `producer_loop` (crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs:272-643) sends one report back for unmet criteria, unchanged files, replay, gate, mirror drift, scope and changelog. It never runs Athena's configured checks (fmt, clippy, test). Those run only in `check_and_verify` (run/mod.rs:1865), after the candidate is built. So a failing gate or an unmet command criterion is first seen by the verifier and costs the whole job. The fix is at that origin, in the one existing send-back. After each producer report, once the formatter has run and the change list is non-empty, a new `Athena::pre_verdict_checks` (run/checks.rs) runs the capability's configured checks on the producer's work tree through `run_check`. It builds in the producer's own `Side::Produce` directory, under a `Class::Producer` slot as `loop_replay` does (run/mod.rs:2341), and applies the path-skip rule through `routing::route`. Each failed check joins `problems` and `report_problems`. A short form (name, command, exit status) goes into the stored attempt `detail` (producer.rs:559) and the UI line. The full command, exit status and last output lines go into the send-back brief through a new `append_failed_checks` in send_back.rs, shaped like `append_mirror_drift`. No new loop or limit: the failure shares the `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1` slot. A check still failing after the send-back stays in `report_problems`, so it reaches the verifier through the existing `producer-report-gaps` entry (verification.rs:97-112). The producer is told in producer.md and in the producer brief. Nothing is refused, so the expected share of newly refused past readings is 0%. Revision answers: (1) and (2) criteria 7 and 8 now name their seam: the refusal gate `refusing_check` over the stored corpus, and the three recorded checks run on the final tree. All commands are single simple commands, with no `&&` chains. (3) docs/system-facts.md is no longer touched: the producer.md edit pays for its addition with a removal, so the computed producer set stays at 1043 and the facts line stays true. Every file in the plan is a listed deliverable.

decisions.choice: Run the configured checks inside the producer loop after each report and fold a failure into the existing single send-back (shared `send_backs` counter, `problems`, `attempt.detail`, brief via an `append_*` function).
decisions.reason: The stage that lacks the information is the producer, and it is the only stage that can repair while it holds its work tree. The loop already collects every pre-verdict problem into one send-back (producer.rs:499-643), so one more problem gives the information with no new budget. `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` (run/mod.rs:1591) stays 1.

rejected.option: A new repair loop after verification, or raising PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS
rejected.why: Out of scope, and it costs a verifier run per miss, which is the failure being fixed.

rejected.option: A refusal rule that refuses a job whose report lacks per-criterion evidence
rejected.why: The request prefers giving the stage the information, and the producer can be given the check output instead. It would also refuse readings.

rejected.option: Move the verification checks earlier and reuse their result at verification
rejected.why: Verification runs in the verifier's snapshot with the base's tool configuration, with CI reuse, slots and a disk gate (run/mod.rs:1976-2092). Reusing a producer-tree result would weaken that independence. The pre-verdict run is advisory and the verifier's run stays authoritative.

decisions.choice: Run every non-skipped configured check in order and do not stop at the first failure.
decisions.reason: The send-back is single-shot, so it must carry everything the producer can fix. Verification's `run_local` stops at the first failure only because it is judging.

rejected.option: Stop at the first failure like `run_local` (routing.rs:182-197)
rejected.why: A clippy failure would hide a test failure and the one send-back would be spent on half the picture.

decisions.choice: Do not call `disk_gate` and do not read `check_seam`. Take a `Class::Producer` slot like `loop_replay`; when the slot wait expires, skip the checks with one UI line. A slot wait is never a hold here.
decisions.reason: `disk_gate` frees idle build directories and some test free-space readers key on `target/produce`. `check_seam` (run/mod.rs:1518) is read in `SnapExec::exec`, and reading it here would give every seam-based test a second fake run. Real `sh -c` checks drive the new tests.

rejected.why: Its `exec` calls `restore_to(prepared)`, which would reset the producer's tree (checks.rs:139-142).

rejected.option: Hold the job on slot wait as `check_and_verify` does
rejected.why: The verifier-side check still runs later and holds if needed. `loop_replay` already treats a slot wait as a skip (run/mod.rs:2344).

decisions.choice: The stored event is the attempt invocation's `detail`, which names each failed check with its command and exit status. The full output tail goes only into the brief. A passing run prints no UI line and writes nothing.
decisions.reason: The `produce_and_verify_order_tests` characterization asserts exactly 8 UI lines and invocation seqs 1, 2, 3 for a passing job (tests.rs:1068). `report_gaps` is stored in the resume mark (state.rs:497), so it takes the short form.

rejected.option: Print a `checks in the loop: ok` line on every pass
rejected.why: It breaks the 8-line order test and adds nothing the verifier's `checks` line does not.

rejected.option: Put the whole output tail in `detail` and `report_gaps`
rejected.why: It bloats the invocation record and the resume mark.

decisions.choice: A check still failing after the send-back stays in `report_problems`, so it reaches the verifier as a `producer-report-gaps` entry; the verifier's own recorded check results still decide the verdict.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks that it be flagged, not hidden. The mechanism exists (producer.rs:521, 576-583; verification.rs:97-112).

rejected.why: A second flagging channel for the same purpose.

decisions.choice: Skip the pre-verdict run for a nested run (`self.nested.is_some()`), a pinned study (`ctx.pin_dir.is_some()`) and an empty change list.
decisions.reason: A nested run's checks belong to the outer job (checks.rs:542-545). `format_stage` skips pinned studies because a mounted checkout sits in the work tree (producer.rs:179). An empty change list fails below as an idle producer. The test `Docs` capability does not pin (`pin_repo` returns None unless `pins_repo()`, pin.rs:39), so the new tests run the checks.

rejected.why: It would run checks in a mounted checkout and waste a run on an idle producer.

decisions.choice: The decision entry is D182 (D181 is the last, decisions.md:5227). It amends D113 (the producer need not run the suite because Athena runs it on the candidate) and D103 (the gaps entry), with matching [[link]] entries in docs/decision-links.toml whose `line` equals the line of the amend phrase.
decisions.reason: Both decisions change in meaning. The link list is a listed deliverable, and its header (decision-links.toml:9-10, 22-23) requires `line` to match. No [[governs]] path is touched.

rejected.option: Edit D103 or D113 in place
rejected.why: The log is append-only and edits to past entries are out of scope.

decisions.choice: Edit producer.md bullet 9 so the producer set keeps its computed size, 1043 tokens. Pay for the added sentence by trimming words elsewhere in that file. The budgets test is the feedback: the producer adjusts wording until `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` passes with docs/system-facts.md unchanged.
decisions.reason: The facts line `budget producer: 1043 of 1200` is compared for equality with the computed value (budgets.rs:109-114). The estimator is ⌈bytes/3⌉ (lib.rs:74-76), so the size is held by keeping the set's byte total in its current 3-byte bucket. lib.rs:177-179 says a set that outgrows its budget pays for the addition with a removal. This keeps docs/system-facts.md out of the change, as finding 3 asks. PRODUCER_FRAME's version stays 1 (lib.rs:45-49). demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree no pre-verdict run exists. The producer is invoked once, the second prompt never exists, and no invocation detail names a failed check. The new tests fail to find `## Sent back` with the check output.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go` -> `produce_and_verify` -> `producer_loop` -> new `Athena::pre_verdict_checks` (step 3). Guards: not nested, no pin_dir, non-empty change list, formatter already run. Fixture: the existing `Docs` capability in `produce_and_verify_order_tests` (tests.rs:91-167), whose single check is named `probe`, with a new `FAILS_WHILE_BROKEN` check const (`sh -c 'if grep -q BROKEN README.md; then echo CHECK-OUTPUT-CANARY; exit 1; fi'`). It passes on the base README. Injected by passing it to `athena_with(repo, state, check, free_space, script)` (exists, tests.rs:191). The fake producer is `fixing_on_send_back` (exists, tests.rs:3311) over `editing` (tests.rs:3066): pass one adds `BROKEN` to README.md, and the pass whose prompt contains `## Sent back` rewrites it clean. `run_check` runs the real `sh`. The new helper `check_job` (step 8) copies `mirror_job` (tests.rs:3333) with the check given by the caller. The logic under test, `pre_verdict_checks`, is production code and is not in the fake.

demonstrations.method: `pre_verdict_a_check_that_fails_on_the_first_pass_is_repaired_on_the_send_back_and_the_job_lands` runs the criterion 2 fixture end to end: the first pass breaks the README, the send-back pass fixes it, and the verifier runs on the clean tree.
demonstrations.observes: Producer invocations 2 and verifier 1, the closing state is `OutcomeState::Landed`, and the UI has a line starting `producer   sent back: ` that names the `probe` check.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree there is no pre-verdict run: the producer is invoked once, the verifier runs on the failing tree and the job is Rejected. The assertions `(producer, verifier) == (2, 1)` and `Landed` fail.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 2: `Athena::go` over the `Docs` capability injected through `athena_with`, `FAILS_WHILE_BROKEN`, and `fixing_on_send_back` with a fix that restores the README (exists, tests.rs:3311). The verifier prompts are captured by a wrapper around the script that keeps `spec.user_prompt` when `spec.role == Role::Verifier` (pattern: `verifier_prompts` in `ci_run`, around tests.rs:7578). The wrapper and `check_job` are added in step 8.

demonstrations.method: `pre_verdict_checks_that_pass_cause_no_send_back_and_no_extra_run` runs the same fixture with the check `PASSES` (`true`) and the `editing` script, with no fix. Also run the existing characterization test with `cargo test -p athena-core a_fake_job_takes_its_baseline_before_the_producer_and_numbers_the_invocations_in_order`, which asserts 8 UI lines and invocation seqs 1, 2, 3 (tests.rs:1068).
demonstrations.observes: Producer 1 and verifier 1, no producer prompt contains `## Sent back`, no UI line contains `sent back`, and the state is Landed. The existing 8-line order test still passes unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the step sent back on a pass, printed a line or added an invocation, the new test and the existing order test would fail on the producer count, the UI line count or the invocation seqs.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` as in criterion 2, guards unchanged. Fixture: `athena_with(.., PASSES, ..)` with the existing `editing` script (exists, tests.rs:3066, 191). The test is added in step 8; no new seam beyond `check_job`.

demonstrations.method: `pre_verdict_a_check_still_failing_after_the_send_back_reaches_the_verifier_flagged` uses `fixing_on_send_back` with an empty fix, so the check fails on both passes. Then `git diff -- crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs` shows only a doc comment near `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` and no new constant.
demonstrations.observes: Producer invocations 2 (bounded by `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`, so no second send-back). The verifier prompt carries a `producer-report-gaps` entry naming `probe`. The verdict is still decided by the recorded check, and the constant remains `const PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS: u32 = 1;`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the flagging, the verifier prompt has no `producer-report-gaps` entry for the check. A second send-back (a new limit) would make the producer count 3.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 3: `Athena::go`, `athena_with`, `FAILS_WHILE_BROKEN`, `fixing_on_send_back` with an empty fix (exists, tests.rs:3311) and the verifier-prompt wrapper (step 8). The constant at run/mod.rs:1591 exists.

demonstrations.method: Run `cargo test -p athena-context producer_brief_tells` first. The new briefs.rs test `producer_brief_tells_the_producer_athena_runs_the_checks_before_the_verifier` renders `producer_brief` from the inputs helper the nearby tests use (around briefs.rs:1564) and asserts that the text after `## Checks Athena will run` says Athena runs the configured checks on the work tree before the verifier and sends a failure back once. Then run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`. The new `producer_prompt_says_athena_runs_the_checks_before_the_verifier` composes the producer set and asserts the producer.md wording and `check_budget(BudgetSet::Producer, ..)`. `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (budgets.rs:125) stays green with docs/system-facts.md unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass, the producer set stays at 1043 of 1200, and `git diff --stat` does not list docs/system-facts.md.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the edits the new briefs.rs and budgets.rs tests fail on the missing sentence. A producer.md edit that changed the set size would fail `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `athena_context::briefs::producer_brief` (briefs.rs:676-751) and `compose`/`check_budget` over `PRODUCER_FRAME` (budgets.rs:357-371), all existing. Fixtures: the producer-brief inputs helper in briefs.rs tests (exists) and `athena_cli::wiring::capabilities()` (budgets.rs:42). The new tests are added in steps 5 and 6.

demonstrations.method: Run the refusal corpus test, then `git diff --stat` and check that the diff touches no file of the gate: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, crates/athena-core/src/reading/, crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs, crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs or crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs. The change adds no parser, stem list, stop list or reading check, so no input form needs a corpus case. The expected share of newly refused past readings is 0%.
demonstrations.observes: `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` and `the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case` pass unchanged: every stored case gets the outcome it had, so nothing accepted before is refused now. The diff stat lists none of the gate files.
demonstrations.fails_without: A refusal check added to the gate would turn a corpus Accept case into a refusal, so `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` would list it in `mismatches`. A new `check_*` step with no refusing case would fail the corpus's coverage test.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `athena_core::reading::refusing_check` (the gate that `check_reading_acceptance` wraps), called by `run(c)` in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs:2770-2778. Fixture: the stored corpus `cases()` (refusal_corpus.rs:303), injected by direct call with each case's reading, request and referenced jobs. The seam exists (read at refusal_corpus.rs:2747-2838). The producer and verifier run it; no step adds it.

demonstrations.method: Run on the final tree, each as its own command: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. These are the three checks Athena records, configured at athena.toml:92-108. Also run `cargo test -p athena-core` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle` while working, so the tests that count producer invocations (FAILS_ON_EDIT users) are adjusted in step 8, not skipped.
demonstrations.observes: All three commands exit 0, including `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`, the decision-link tests and the lifecycle tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: Any fmt, clippy or test failure fails this. The cases most likely to fail are tests whose check fails after the producer's edit (they now get one extra send-back), and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` if the producer.md edit changed the set size.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the three cargo commands in the capability's configured checks (athena.toml `[[capabilities.change.checks]]`), which Athena runs through `run_check` at verification (checks.rs:513). Fixture: the final tree itself; there is no double. They exist today, so no step adds them.
